engines_meta.stress_handling: U+0301 survives the repo's text pipeline (robust cleanup + WeText) unchanged. It is NOT a SentencePiece vocab piece: byte fallback encodes each mark as the byte pair <0xCC><0x81>, so marks reach the model as bytes (no [UNK], no dropping). Measured: all marked sentence pairs give different audio; unmarked controls (#25, #28) are byte-identical across runs. Separate finding: with WeText ON (repo default), pure-Cyrillic text is routed to WeText's Chinese grammar — digits become Chinese numerals («3 бра́та» → «三 бра́та», «01.09.2026 в 14:30» → «二零二六年九月一日 в 十四点三十分»); the voice config '+no-wetext' turns it off.

engines_meta.stress_handling: No stress model and no Russian normalization in the frontend (NFKD + symbol cleanup; digits passed raw). U+0301 is a known symbol (unicode_indexer index 146) and reaches the model; NFKD also decomposes ё → е + U+0308 (index 152). Stage A: in all 4 neutral minimal pairs (за́мок/замо́к, му́ка/мука́, а́тлас/атла́с, пла́чу/плачу́; shared seed) the unmarked versions are byte-identical and moving the mark changes the audio; removing marks changes the audio in 21/22 items; unmarked control identical. Marks also lengthen the predicted duration slightly (e.g. S05 4.25 vs 3.97 s), but within a minimal pair (same length) duration is identical — the change comes from the mark position. Stage B corpus: 60/60 marked pairs differ.

Provenance/licence: research-purpose OpenRAIL-M fine-tune, base licence stated inconsistently (MIT vs CC-BY-4.0), Russian training data not listed. Runtime: the checkpoint (simba9/voxtream2-ru) and its RUAccent/RUNorm models are huggingface.co-only (large files refused here; no modelscope.cn mirror); it also pulls herimor/voxtream2, kyutai Mimi and IDRnD/ReDimNet; the card asks for a GPU (~4 GB VRAM).
blocker.unblock: Clarify licence and training data with the author; allow huggingface.co large-file CDNs; a GPU is recommended.
